extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, auditors, and securities/transaction attorneys preparing SEC filings involving business combinations (Rule 3-05/20-F/Reg S-X)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on determining when an acquiree is a 'foreign business', what bases of accounting are acceptable for Rule 3-05 financial statements, reconciliation and age/currency/period requirements, and related SEC/Form 20-F filing considerations for acquisitions and carve-outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign business definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A business that is majority owned by persons who are not citizens or residents of the United States and is not organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof, and either (1) more than 50 percent of its assets are located outside the United States; or (2) the majority of its executive officers and directors are not United States citizens or residents. [S-X Rule 1.02(l)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining majority ownership, the SEC staff will consider the ultimate parent entity that would consolidate the business under US GAAP (or IFRS-IASB for IFRS issuers) and the parent's controlling shareholders. The section illustrates application via examples (e.g., US parent with non-US subsidiaries is not a foreign business; holdings with >50% assets outside US may be presumed not organized in the US).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of foreign business definition to carve-outs
rubrics_metrics.description: A carved-out reporting entity is presumed to be US-organized (and not a foreign business) if (a) the entity is a carve-out entirely from an entity incorporated in the US; or (b) the entity comprises components of subsidiaries, or is carved out from businesses that are subsidiaries of a US company, regardless of tier or organization country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither presumption applies and the carve-out comprises entities organized both in and outside the US, apply all elements of the foreign business definition to the facts and circumstances, including: relative significance of parts organized in and outside the US and majority ownership (considering the ultimate consolidating parent and its controlling shareholders). If a presumption is present but the registrant believes it is overcome, consult legal counsel and consider discussing facts with the SEC staff. Examples illustrate when a carve-out is considered organized in the US (e.g., carve-out entirely from a US-incorporated subsidiary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to determine whether an acquiree is a foreign business
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no specified rule date; registrants should use the date that makes the most sense based on individual facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible assessment dates include: end of the acquiree’s most recently completed fiscal year; the filing date of a pre-consummation registration statement/proxy (potentially re-calculated as of effective/mailing date); immediately before reporting consummation on Form 8-K (Item 2.01); or the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter (similar to FPI status determination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable bases for Rule 3-05 financial statements when the acquiree does not meet 'foreign business' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-tree outcomes depend on whether the acquiree would qualify as a foreign private issuer (FPI) if it were a registrant and whether the registrant is an FPI that prepares under IFRS-IASB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquiree would not qualify as an FPI: Rule 3-05 statements must be prepared under US GAAP or other GAAP reconciled to US GAAP (reconciliation per Item 18 of Form 20-F). If it would qualify as an FPI and the registrant is not an IFRS-IASB preparer: statements may be US GAAP, IFRS-IASB, or home-country GAAP reconciled to either US GAAP or IFRS-IASB (reconciling per Item 17). If registrant is an IFRS-IASB-preparing FPI: statements may be US GAAP, IFRS-IASB, or home-country GAAP reconciled to US GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable bases for Rule 3-05 financial statements when the acquiree meets 'foreign business' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquiree is a foreign business, acceptable bases depend on whether the registrant is an FPI that prepares under IFRS-IASB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant is not an IFRS-IASB-preparing FPI: Rule 3-05 statements may be prepared under US GAAP, IFRS-IASB, or home-country GAAP reconciled to either US GAAP or IFRS-IASB (reconciliation per Item 17). If registrant is an IFRS-IASB-preparing FPI: Rule 3-05 statements may be prepared under US GAAP, IFRS-IASB, or home-country GAAP reconciled to US GAAP (reconciliation per Item 17). A domestic registrant or FPI may file Rule 3-05 statements based on IFRS-IASB without reconciliation to US GAAP, regardless of acquisition significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 20-F reconciliation levels (Item 17 vs Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 17 requires: (a) a qualitative discussion of material variations between the accounting principles used and US GAAP/Reg S-X and (b) a quantitative reconciliation of such material variations. Item 18 requires Item 17 information plus disclosures required by US GAAP and Reg S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Item 17 applies but the acquisition is not greater than 30% significant, the quantitative reconciliation is not required (only qualitative disclosure) — except this 30% accommodation does not apply when Rule 3-05 statements are filed on Form S-4, Form F-4 or a proxy statement for a nonreporting foreign target (then quantitative reconciliation is required). A US GAAP reconciliation must be included unless unavailable or not obtainable without unreasonable cost/expense; unavailability is a very high hurdle and pre-clearance is recommended. If reconciliation is unavailable, narrative disclosure of all material variations is required. The reconciliation exception does not apply to pro forma financial information under S-X Article 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFRS 1 applicability on first-time reconciliation to IFRS-IASB
rubrics_metrics.description: IFRS 1, First-time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards, is applicable when an acquired business’s financial statements are being reconciled to IFRS-IASB for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply IFRS 1 because an entity reconciling to IFRS for the first time faces similar challenges to one directly presenting under IFRS for the first time. Example: an FPI preparing an F-4 including two years audited financials with reconciliation from home-country GAAP to IFRS applying IFRS 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of IFRS for SMEs in Rule 3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted only in limited circumstances: an acquired business that meets the definition of a foreign business may base its financial statements on the IFRS for SMEs Accounting Standard but must reconcile to US GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff will not accept SMEs-based financial statements for issuers, predecessors of issuers, domestic acquired businesses, or domestic equity-method investees. [FRM 6410.6(d)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Staff Accounting Bulletins (SABs) to Rule 3-05 statements not based on US GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: SABs related to filing and audit requirements apply to all Rule 3-05 financial statements, even if not based on US GAAP. Financial statements not based on US GAAP need not reflect SABs that are US GAAP specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff’s expectation is that IFRS-IASB financial statements filed with the SEC have considered and applied other relevant SAB topics (e.g., those related to IFRS, filing requirements, materiality). Entities may elect to apply SABs where their GAAP lacks guidance (e.g., extractive activities); if electing SAB guidance, provide full, transparent disclosures about selected accounting policies and their effects consistent with IAS 1 and IAS 8. See FRM 6320.4–.5 and FRM 6320.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency to use in Rule 3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 financial statements may be prepared either in the same currency as the registrant or in the currency normally used to prepare the acquiree’s or registrant’s financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For significance tests, the acquiree’s financial information should be converted to the registrant’s currency. (S-X Rule 3-20 allows FPIs to prepare financial statements in the currency they believe appropriate, but it does not address acquirees; FRM 6620.7.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of annual periods required under Rule 3-05 (period requirements by significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05(b) sets the annual period requirements (same for domestic and foreign acquirees): acquisitions 20% or less significant — no periods required; greater than 20% up to 40% — one annual period required; greater than 40% — two annual periods required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule also addresses interim period requirements (see referenced Question 4.2.20 for interim periods). Examples illustrate application (e.g., 25% significant acquisition requires one annual period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirements for Rule 3-05 financial statements of foreign businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquiree meets the definition of a foreign business, the age of financial statements filed is determined under Item 8 of Form 20-F (not under S-X Rules 3-01 and 3-02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 8.A sets age requirements including: last year of audited financial statements may not be older than 15 months at time of offering/listing (12 months for initial public offering at filing); if document is dated more than nine months after the end of the last audited financial year, consolidated interim financial statements (may be unaudited) covering at least the first six months should be included with comparative prior period information and selected note disclosures. Companies are encouraged (but not required) to have interim statements reviewed by an independent auditor; if reviewed, include the auditor’s interim review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and basis requirements for acquirees that are domestic or do not meet the foreign business definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The age requirements of Rule 3-05 financial statements of a domestic entity acquired by an FPI are the same as those for a domestic entity acquired by a domestic registrant; the same age requirements apply to a foreign entity that does not meet the definition of a foreign business. These age requirements reside in S-X Rule 3-01 and Rule 3-02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an acquiree does not meet the foreign business definition, treat age and other procedural requirements per the cited S-X rules (see section 4.2.10 for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of US GAAP financial statements for foreign acquirees
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 8 of Form 20-F allows financial statements of foreign entities filed in the US to be based on US GAAP regardless of whether the foreign acquiree meets the definition of a foreign business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US GAAP financial statements are acceptable even if the registrant prepares its financial statements on a non-US GAAP basis. However, to perform significance tests the acquiree’s financial information must be converted to the registrant’s basis for preparing financial statements (see section 6.3.10).
